images.note: Beat: Box 4 — Bryan at 36, Democratic nominee after the Cross of Gold speech; Populist fusion (Bryan for president / Tom Watson for VP). Full magazine page (8360x11776, 4.6MB); Bryan portrait is the top-left image, captioned 'WILLIAM JENNINGS BRYAN. Democratic Candidate for President. — From a Photograph by Bell.' Published 8 days after his July 10 nomination — fully contemporary. Alt: none qualifying — the obvious Library of Congress 1896 Bryan photograph (loc.gov/item/2018757413) scans at only 437x640px, failing the 1200px gate; no second institutional source found at bar.
images.source: Internet Archive — Harper's Weekly, July 18, 1896, p.700 (Harper & Brothers)
images.title: William Jennings Bryan, Democratic presidential candidate, 1896

images.note: Beat: Box 4 — McKinley (Ohio governor): gold standard, high tariff, 'full dinner pail'; Mark Hanna's corporate money machine behind him. Cover engraving (4040x6016, 1.75MB) captioned 'WILLIAM McKINLEY, REPUBLICAN CANDIDATE FOR PRESIDENT. Engraved by E. Schladitz from a copyrighted photograph by Courtney, Canton, Ohio, April 1896.' Contemporary April 1896 photograph, published 9 days after the St. Louis convention. Scan is dark (typical of the engraving) but legible. Alt: none qualifying — LOC 1896 McKinley portraits scan at ~480x640px, failing the 1200px gate.
images.source: Internet Archive — Harper's Weekly, June 27, 1896, cover (Harper & Brothers)
images.title: William McKinley, Republican presidential candidate, 1896

images.note: Beats: Box 4 (Cross of Gold / Chicago convention, July 1896) AND Box 3 free-silver demand. Full page (8189x11768, 4.8MB): 'SCENES AT THE DEMOCRATIC NATIONAL CONVENTION, CHICAGO, ILLINOIS. — Drawn by T. Dart Walker.' Six vignettes incl. '1. Discussing Gold and Silver in the Corridors of the Palmer House,' '2. 16 to 1 — A Study in Hats and Whiskers' (direct visual for the Omaha Platform's 16:1 free-silver demand), '5. W. J. Bryan carried on the shoulders of his admirers.' Contemporary eyewitness illustration, published 8 days after the convention. Alt: none — no second institutional source for this specific illustration at bar.
images.source: Internet Archive — Harper's Weekly, July 18, 1896, p.701 (Harper & Brothers)
images.title: Scenes at the Democratic National Convention, Chicago, July 1896

images.note: Beat: Box 4 — the Panic of 1893 ('the floor fell out'; four-year financial crisis; Cleveland clung to the gold standard; 'Washington worked for the bankers'). Full page (7889x11914, 5.8MB): 'COXEY'S ARMY APPROACHING WASHINGTON, APRIL 30th' (top: 'Marshal Carl Browne on his charger'; 'General Coxey, accompanied by reporters with bicycles') and ''GENERAL' COXEY ESCORTED FROM THE CAPITOL. From sketches by T. Dart Walker' (large bottom illustration of the march at the Capitol). Contemporary eyewitness sketches of the unemployed workers' march — the human face of the depression that radicalized the farmers. Alt: none qualifying — LOC Coxey's Army photos (cph.3c05022 etc.) scan at ~512x640px, failing the 1200px gate.
images.source: Internet Archive — Harper's Weekly, May 12, 1894, p.456 (Harper & Brothers)
images.title: Coxey's Army approaching Washington and escorted from the Capitol, April–May 1894

images.note: Beat: Box 4 — the Wizard of Oz allegory (Maya's memory device: Dorothy's silver shoes = free silver; Scarecrow = farmer; Tin Man = factory worker; Cowardly Lion = Bryan). Genuine 1900 first-edition cover (2586x3436, 1.5MB): 'The WONDERFUL WIZARD of OZ / BY L. FRANK BAUM / PICTURES BY W. W. DENSLOW' with Denslow's Cowardly Lion. Script voices the allegory with the 'whether Baum meant it, historians still argue' hedge — the cover is the correct visual anchor. Alt: none — no second institutional source for the first-edition cover at bar.
